questions.title: Classifying the knee joint
questions.question: How is the knee joint anatomically classified based on its movement type?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A pivot joint allows rotation only around a single axis, as at the joint between the first two cervical vertebrae — not the knee's flexion/extension-dominated movement.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A ball-and-socket joint, like the hip or shoulder, allows free movement in all planes — far more range than the knee permits.
explanations.C: Correct. By movement type, the knee is classed as a modified hinge (ginglymus) joint. It mainly performs flexion and extension, like a pure hinge such as the elbow, but it permits a small amount of rotation as well once the joint is flexed. A pure hinge, by contrast, allows no such rotary component.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A saddle joint, like the joint at the base of the thumb, allows movement in two perpendicular planes without full rotation — a different movement profile from the knee's modified-hinge action.

questions.learning_objective: Classify the knee as a modified hinge joint, distinct from a pure hinge, ball-and-socket, or pivot joint.
